answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable onyx bond before it may sign work, so creating fake identities costs real capital. A peer who catches a duplicate signs a quill attestation proving the reuse, and the bond of the copy is slashed while the honest reporter earns a share. Honest agents keep a haven of low-value trades where one bond covers many small jobs, while an attacker must post a fresh bond for every fake identity, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand bonds and the attack stops paying.
